Use case: compositing. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop. Image2 provides mascot identity and anatomy only. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion where the human anatomy becomes a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body. The face must feature green-ringed black eyes and a source-matching closed mouth, preserving the serious expression. Retain the actual source hair: strongly receding bare upper crown with sparse short grey-brown side hair and visible brow hair. Do not invent a moustache, beard, cap, or spectacles; the chin is smooth and distinct. Preserve the dark grey open-lapel pinstripe suit, white shirt, and pale gold patterned tie. No invented hidden lapel decorations. The rounded chin must immediately meet a raised, broadened existing neckline with a very short, broad neck transition and minimal throat exposure. Avoid separate yellow neck shafts, pointed V funnels, pinched collars, neck rolls, floating collars, clipping, or cream belly bibs. Maintain coherent front/rear collar overlap and contact shadows. Retain the complete tilted dark frame, opaque photographic backing in its exact original color, and the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. No invented insignia, text, or accessories. Fine primary details that are indistinct in the source must remain understated.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: Bareheaded nearly frontal serious CLOSED-MOUTH bust, strongly receding/bare upper crown with sparse short GREY-BROWN side hair and actual brow HAIR, smooth chin and no visible distinct moustache. Dark grey OPEN-lapel PINSTRIPE suit, white shirt and pale GOLD/YELLOW patterned tie beside note; do not invent hidden lapel decorations. No cap, spectacles or beard. Preserve primary head angle, light and crop.
Mascot green-ringed black eyes and real source eyebrow hair retained. Preserve exact source head angle and expression. Whole yellow area above raised/broadened neckline is one compact near-round head, with clearly rounded chin immediately contacting the very short broad collar transition, no additional separate neck shaft or pointed V. Image1 is the exact original small card; Image2 identity only. Fine markings indistinct in Image1 must remain understated, not invented as a readable symbol.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
